- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices during bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.20) — add 3–5% to forecast to compensate.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is consistently positive over last 5 days (overconfidence bias).
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior, forecast should be slightly higher than baseline — but not exceed 10% above recent 14-day average.
